clue.text: Lighten a wicked vile tale

indicators.note: wicked suggests something perverted or bent out of its proper shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants to tone down a nasty, wicked story.
explanation.definitionFit: To alleviate pain or worry is to ease it, to make the burden lighter.

clue.text: Ardent Liberal fuelling a reputation

indicators.note: fuel is fed into something, so one piece is put inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for Liberal
fame is renown, public reputation

explanation.surface: A passionate Liberal politician stoking someone's renown.
explanation.definitionFit: Aflame describes burning with passion, figuratively as ardent as a fire.

clue.text: Start smoking in open view at college

blocks.note: to bring into the light is to put on open view
a student is said to be up at university

explanation.surface: A student lights a cigarette openly on campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at Oxford or Cambridge means in residence there, a British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: To light up is to ignite a cigarette or pipe and begin to smoke.

clue.text: Quantitative data Miss World will have supplied?

blocks.note: first meaning: official figures on births, deaths and marriages
second meaning: a woman's bust, waist and hip measurements, as beauty contestants once gave

explanation.walkthrough: Miss World is the beauty pageant; contestants' measurements were famously quoted. The question mark marks this playful second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both population figures and, jokingly, a woman's body measurements.

clue.text: Suddenly everyone's in agreement, including Conservative's leader

indicators.note: the leader is the front one, so just the opening letter is kept
including means taking another piece inside

blocks.note: all at one means everyone agrees
the first letter of the party name

explanation.surface: Everyone suddenly agrees, the Tory leader included.
explanation.walkthrough: The C sits between ALL AT ON and E.
explanation.definitionFit: All at once means abruptly and without warning, just as suddenly does.

clue.text: Provide witty remark after end of joke

indicators.note: the end means only the last letter of the following word is kept

blocks.note: final letter of the word
a quip is a witty remark

explanation.surface: Someone supplies a clever comeback once the joke is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the remark after the single letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to provide or supply them with what they need.

clue.text: Put a price on a rib

blocks.note: to cost something is to put a price on it
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is valuing a cut of meat, a rib, for sale.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the anatomical sense: costa is the Latin-derived term for a rib.
explanation.definitionFit: Costa is the anatomical and botanical term for a rib, as in the adjective costal.

clue.text: A period required after to reach end

definitions.text: A period required after to reach end

blocks.note: surface reading: some length of time is needed afterwards
setter's reading: a period is the American word for the punctuation mark that ends a sentence, which is where a sentence arrives at its finish

explanation.surface: Some time must pass afterwards before things can wind up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Period' looks like a span of time, but it is the punctuation mark the British call a full stop.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to stop completely, as a sentence does at its closing punctuation.

clue.text: Filthy group of soldiers briefly given cover

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a squad is a small unit of soldiers
a lid is a cover

explanation.surface: A dirty army unit is given shelter for a short while.
explanation.definitionFit: Squalid describes surroundings that are dirty and wretched, filthy.

clue.text: Religious retreat in wood run by a spymaster

blocks.note: ash is a type of tree and its timber
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
taken as written
M is the head of MI6 in the James Bond stories

explanation.surface: A spy chief manages a secluded holy hideaway in a forest.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashram is a Hindu hermitage or community for religious retreat.

clue.text: To walk or run away is acceptable

blocks.note: first meaning: a two-word informal verb for making off on foot
second meaning: the one-word slang adjective for above board

explanation.walkthrough: Read as two words the answer is the British slang for running off; read as one it is slang for legitimate.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg it is informal for walking briskly or fleeing, while legit is short for legitimate, meaning genuine and allowable.

clue.text: Braggart in flash trap

blocks.note: flash and loud both describe showy, garish clothes
trap is slang for the mouth, as in 'shut your trap'

explanation.surface: A show-off gets caught in a flashy trap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' only joins definition to wordplay; it is not a container signal here.
explanation.definitionFit: A loudmouth talks too much and too boastfully, which is what a braggart does.

clue.text: Friend goes with many a sailor

blocks.note: mate is an everyday word for a friend
a lot means many

explanation.surface: A pal tags along with a crowd of seafarers.
explanation.definitionFit: Matelot is British informal slang, borrowed from French, for a seaman.

clue.text: A command to break old man's kneecap

indicators.note: to break into something is to split it open with something else lodged inside

blocks.note: pa is a familiar name for one's father
taken as written
to tell someone to do something is to command them

explanation.surface: A sinister order to smash an elderly man's knee.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces A and TELL go inside the old man, splitting him P...A.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the anatomical name for the kneecap bone.

clue.text: Undertake a task till . . .?

annotation.answer: PUT ONE'S HAND TO THE PLOUGH

blocks.note: surface reading: commit to a piece of work
setter's reading: till is a verb meaning to work the soil, and the ellipsis leaves the phrase to be finished with the farm implement that does so

explanation.surface: Someone starts on a job and works at it until it is done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Till' looks like the word for 'until', but here it is the farming verb, and the farming idiom completes it.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical idiom means to commit oneself to a task, pictured as starting to work a field.

clue.text: Sailor about to collect special gunpowder ingredient

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an old salt is a seasoned sailor
re means concerning, about
a pet project is a special favourite

explanation.surface: A sailor is about to gather a special component for gunpowder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sailor about' is one unit that does the collecting; 'about' is the short word for concerning, not a reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saltpetre, potassium nitrate, is the oxidising ingredient of black gunpowder.

clue.text: Creeping plant in home on wheels

blocks.note: first meaning: a plant that trails along the ground
second meaning: a caravan towed behind a vehicle

explanation.surface: A climbing plant growing inside a caravan.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a trailing plant and a towed mobile home, especially in American usage.

clue.text: A number, following try, cheer

indicators.note: following tells us the words before it come second in the answer, after the next piece

blocks.note: a judge tries, or hears, a case
ten is a number

explanation.surface: A number of supporters, after an attempt, raise a cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the number after the court verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To hearten someone is to cheer them up and give them encouragement.

clue.text: Bishop, encouraged, asked for money

blocks.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
egged on means urged or encouraged

explanation.surface: A bishop, spurred on, makes a request for funds.
explanation.definitionFit: To beg is to plead for charity, typically money, from passers-by.

clue.text: One who instructs cashier

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who tells others what to do
second meaning: a bank clerk who handles money

explanation.surface: A trainer teaching a new bank clerk.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both one who tells or orders and a bank employee serving customers.

clue.text: Went by, pleased for a change

indicators.note: a change means the order of these letters is altered into something new

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone passed by, happy for once.
explanation.definitionFit: Time that has elapsed has passed, gone by.

clue.text: Elizabethan sailor died a dissolute man

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for died
a rake is a man of loose morals

explanation.surface: An Elizabethan seafarer died a debauched man.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Francis Drake was the famous navigator and naval commander under Elizabeth I.

clue.text: Errand boy collecting wicked loot

indicators.note: collecting means gathering something up and holding it within

blocks.note: a page is a boy who runs errands
ill can mean evil, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: A messenger boy gathers up stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Pillage and loot are both verbs for plundering by force.

clue.text: Gad about with suitor round centre of St Ives?

indicators.note: the centre means only the middle letters of the place name are kept
round means one piece surrounds the other

blocks.note: a gallant is a man courting a woman
the middle two of the six letters of St Ives

explanation.surface: A wooer roams around the Cornish seaside town of St Ives.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ives is a resort town in Cornwall; the question mark flags that only its middle letters are wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant and to gad about both mean to roam around looking for fun.

clue.text: Toddler, alone, hasn't one that's full

indicators.note: hasn't means lacking, so these letters are removed from the word before

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
taken as written, to be removed

explanation.surface: A small child left alone and lonely.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ONE from ALONE leaves AL.
explanation.definitionFit: A total eclipse or total failure is complete, entire, full in extent.

clue.text: Girl from Brentford or Isleworth

indicators.note: from means the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of the first place and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A girl from two west London suburbs, Brentford and Isleworth.
explanation.walkthrough: Brentford and Isleworth are neighbouring districts in west London.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris is a traditional female first name, so a girl.

clue.text: Look at key in surprise

blocks.note: to eye something is to look at it
a key is something that opens a lock

explanation.surface: Someone stares at a key in astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a revelation, something that astonishes and enlightens.
